Hi Elena — thanks for sending this over and apologies for the short delay. I’ve pulled together answers to each of the hosted-API items and attached a short summary + a diagram. High level below; see attached PDF for the Q/A table and references to our compliance docs.

High-level answers (hosted API):
- Data residency: Customer requests and responses are stored in US regions by default (us-west-2). Customers can request EU or APAC regional handling for an additional configuration; we support pinning per-tenant at provisioning time.
- Default retention: Request/response payloads are retained for 30 days by default for debugging and quality monitoring. Customers can opt into a shorter retention (7 days) or request deletion-on-receipt for strict-e2e scenarios.
- Deletion flow: Deletion requests trigger a purge job that removes objects from primary object storage and deletes indices from our metadata DB. Purge jobs are idempotent and tracked; we record a deletion audit event in the customer’s audit log.
- Backups & snapshots: Backups are on a 90-day retention schedule for disaster recovery; deleted data is removed from the next scheduled snapshot sweep and older snapshots are rotated per the 90-day window. If you require shorter backup retention or legal holds, we can discuss contract language and a tailored configuration.
- Caching/ephemeral storage: KV caches and inference caches are ephemeral (in-memory or local NVMe) and are evicted on instance restart; these are not persisted to long-term storage.
- Logs & telemetry: Application logs that include request identifiers are retained 365 days in our observability system; they do not contain full request payloads by default. Full payloads are only stored in the request store described above.

I attached: Redwood_TenantSanctuary_Answers.pdf and a data-flow diagram (data-flow-diagram.png). For audit artifacts, we can provide a deletion attestation (signed) and our SOC 2 report through the compliance portal once NDA is in place. Ben is looping in on attestation scope.

If anything here needs more technical detail (e.g., S3 lifecycle timings, exact DB indexes removed), say the word and Marissa can add specifics.

Best,

Hi Elena — Marissa from the infra/compliance engineering team here. Quick answers to your follow-ups: 

1) Backups and key handling:
- Backups: backups/snapshots are encrypted at rest. For our hosted offering, we manage KMS keys; backups contain encrypted payloads. If you require BYOK or customer-controlled keys, that’s supported in Redwood Private (we can scope that separately).
- Key rotation: rotating a KMS key does not affect ability to delete previously encrypted objects — rotation creates new ciphertext for new writes while existing objects remain decryptable under the key rotation policy. Purge jobs delete object metadata and object blobs; we also delete associated encryption metadata where applicable.

2) Deletion attestation format (example):
- Attestation ID: UUID
- Customer: Tenant Sanctuary
- Deletion trigger: API request id or manual ticket number
- Timestamp (ISO8601): when purge job completed
- Storage object IDs: list of object keys/paths removed
- Scope: scope of deletion (request payloads, cached KV entries, indices, backups swept)
- Signer: Redwood compliance lead (signed digital attestation)

We typically provide a compressed CSV or signed JSON manifest with the fields above and a brief narrative describing the purge job. If you want object names redacted in the attestation for privacy, we can provide hash digests instead.

Happy to jump on a short call to walkthrough the attestation format and sample.

—Marissa
